data.text:
I have enough evidence. Key findings from gw.lan:

- `ifconfig vtnet0`: WAN is UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP, status active, has DHCP address 198.51.100.27, default route present (`netstat -rn`).
- `ping` to both the ISP gateway (198.51.100.1) and an internet host fails with `sendto: No buffer space available` — the transmit path is stalled.
- `dmesg -a`: repeated `vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0` plus link DOWN/UP cycles.
- `netstat -i`: vtnet0 shows 48211 Oerrs accumulating.
- `netstat -m`: 0 mbuf/cluster requests denied — not memory exhaustion.
- Modem telemetry: `cm_status: OPERATIONAL`, registration complete (modem recovered after a 02:01 T3 timeout / reboot), so the provider side is fine.
- Watchdog state: 12 reloads in 24h hit the cap; WAN reloads did not restore connectivity.

The internet is down because the firewall's WAN NIC/driver (vtnet0, virtio) is hung — its TX queue times out and packets can't be sent, even though link and addressing are intact. Repeated WAN reloads didn't clear it, so this needs a full interface/host reset.

data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0, virtio) has hung — its TX queue repeatedly hits watchdog timeouts so outbound packets cannot be sent, leaving the internet down despite an active link, valid DHCP address, and an OPERATIONAL modem.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface driver (vtnet0, virtio) has hung — its TX queue repeatedly hits watchdog timeouts so outbound packets cannot be sent, leaving the internet down despite an active link, valid DHCP address, and an OPERATIONAL modem.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' with link DOWN/UP cycles
ping -c 3 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 1.1.1.1 both fail with 'sendto: No buffer space available' (stalled TX path)
netstat -i shows vtnet0 accumulating Oerrs (48211) while Ipkts still rise
ifconfig vtnet0 shows status active/LOWER_UP with IP 198.51.100.27 and netstat -rn shows a default route via 198.51.100.1, so addressing/routing are intact
netstat -m shows 0 mbuf/cluster requests denied, ruling out memory exhaustion
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl and modem-events.jsonl show cm_status OPERATIONAL and registration complete after the 02:01 T3-timeout reboot, so the provider side recovered
/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json shows reloads_in_outage=4 and events.jsonl shows reloads_24h hit max (12) — WAN reloads did not restore connectivity
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 driver/NIC; a plain WAN reload has already been tried repeatedly without effect. The maintainer is away, so proceed under the fallback path if they cannot be reached.
